notes: Open with share and ranking, not acreage alone: Gujarat matters because it over-indexes in multiple national value chains at once. Point to cotton and groundnut as the clearest concentration proof, then use milk and horticulture to show breadth beyond field crops.
title: Gujarat anchors several of India’s highest-value farm value chains, with especially strong national positions in cotton, groundnut, milk, and horticulture
subtitle: The state’s importance is not just cultivated area; it is the concentration of output in commercially integrated crops and perishables that connect farmers to processors, traders, exporters, and dairy networks at national scale.

chart.annotation: Gujarat is not broadly average; it holds outsized national shares in multiple commercial farm chains, led by groundnut and cotton.
chart.source: Source: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, DAHD, NHB 2024-2025 [[src:official]]

insights.text: **Groundnut** is the clearest national concentration point at **35%**[[src:official]] of India output, making Gujarat central to one of the country’s largest oilseed value chains and highly relevant for water-smart crop strategy.

**Cotton** at **30%**[[src:official]] confirms the state’s weight in a major commercial crop that links farm productivity directly to ginning, textiles, export competitiveness, and climate-risk exposure in water-stressed districts.

The contribution is broad, not crop-specific: **Milk** at **8%**[[src:official]] and **Horticulture** at **7%**[[src:official]] show Gujarat also matters in year-round perishables and livestock-linked income systems, expanding the case for value-chain execution beyond staple crop support.

footnote: National output shares are shown to evidence Gujarat’s concentrated importance across commercial crop, dairy, and horticulture value chains. Source: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, National Horticulture Board 2024-2025 [[src:official]]
